items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Slam Stewart in the context of a solo style ('bowing like Slam Stewart'), but the interviewee (Danny Barker) does not mention Slam Stewart, nor does he confirm any personal interaction or relationship with him in the provided text.

ctx.x: Because a dancer can slip on it. He's conscious of it. So he comes ou and he'd see all these little-bitty things on it. "What is all this?" And he'd do it three or four times, and kick them off the stage. He was saying, "What's that? What's all that trash out there?" "Somebody's throwing spitballs." Well, somebody in the band, or Dizzy's throwin' it... And then he's watching for it. So he's in the wings, so he's watching...

Well, what really happened on that particular day was, I was playing this solo, "Girl Of My Dreams," which he had taught me, bowing like Slam Stewart. And I couldn't hear him them flatted fifths too cool. You know, when I got to the end ...[SINGS]..., I missed it a mile. And when I made it, any time I'd make it, did it all right, I'd look back at Diz. If I made it, Diz would say, "Great. You did it great" -- you know. And that day, it was a matinee performance, I missed that thing a mile. And I looked back at…
